guard: `cotal up --max-file-store` renders the cap and nats-server applies it, `down --preserve-state` journals it, a resume asking for a different cap is refused, and the bare resume re-renders the preserved cap (#1888).
why: The suite drives the shipped binary against a real broker and reads the rendered server-open.conf, the nats-server `Max Storage` line, the resume document and the mesh record, so every mutant is observed through what an operator would see.
The CLI resolves its workspace packages from `dist`, so every mutant builds first and `afterRestore` rebuilds.
The first mutant keeps `--max-file-store` accepted and recorded but stops passing it to the renderer, so the cap is silently ignored.

mutations.name: detached boot accepts the flag but does not render it
mutations.find: writeOpenBrokerConf(storeDir, { port, host, transport, maxFileStore: opts.maxFileStore })
mutations.expectRed: the fresh boot renders --max-file-store into the jetstream block
mutations.cell: the fresh boot renders --max-file-store into the jetstream block

mutations.name: the preservation cut does not journal the cap
mutations.find: const cap: { maxFileStore?: number } = mesh.maxFileStore !== undefined ? { maxFileStore: mesh.maxFileStore } : {};
mutations.expectRed: the cut journals the store cap in the preserved launch
mutations.cell: the cut journals the store cap in the preserved launch

mutations.name: a resume with a different cap is not refused
mutations.expectRed: a resume asking for a different --max-file-store is refused
mutations.cell: a resume asking for a different --max-file-store is refused

mutations.name: the resume re-entry drops the preserved cap
mutations.expectRed: the bare resume re-renders the preserved store cap
mutations.cell: the bare resume re-renders the preserved store cap
